flagged.evidence: The item says that over the nonlocal ring "S=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]", the complex "is the minimal free resolution of k" and that the regular-quotient theorem gives that minimal resolution. But def-minimal-free-resolution-over-a-local-ring defines minimality only "over local (R,\mathfrak m)". Its cited cor-complete-intersection-betti-numbers-binomial likewise requires a sequence "in the maximal ideal of a local ring". No graded-minimal convention is stated.

Step 1.1 says: "The H_1=0 hypothesis and the generator homotopies force its residue modulo \mathfrak m to vanish." The opened homotopy dependency proves only that each x_i acts null-homotopically, hence x_iH_q=0. Since x_i\in\mathfrak m, that does not imply H_q/\mathfrak mH_q=0; a nonzero module killed by (\mathbf x) can still have nonzero residue. The opened Nakayama statement requires an established equality \mathfrak mH_q=H_q, which the proof never derives. This skips the substantive rigidity argument needed for the conclusion.

The statement assumes only that (R,\mathfrak m) is local, \mathbf x\subseteq\mathfrak m, and the Koszul complex resolves its quotient, then calls it a "minimal free resolution". It never assumes M finite free. Step 2.1 incorrectly says acyclicity and the degree-zero quotient make it finite free. For R=k[[u,v]], M=(u,v), and x=u, multiplication by u is injective on M and K(u;M) resolves M/uM, but its two terms are M, which is not a free R-module. The cited cor-koszul-complex-resolves-a-regular-quotient explicitly has the additional hypothesis "M is finite free".

The statement says only "In the finite Noetherian-local maximal-ideal setting" that ordinary, Koszul, and H_1 regularity coincide, omitting the nonzero terminal-quotient hypothesis used by its dependency cor-regularity-notions-coincide-local-finite. Take a field R=k with maximal ideal 0, M=0, and the one-term sequence (0)\subseteq\mathfrak m. All Koszul chain groups and hence positive homology vanish, so the sequence is Koszul-regular and H_1-regular; but def-regular-sequence-on-a-module requires M/(0)M\ne0, so it is not ordinarily regular.
